A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research framework and six evaluation domains. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison; visual inspection resolved material missing from text extraction.

before.justification: V1 reports original adaptive-evaluation experiments, forecasting analyses, transfer results, and human validation of generated questions.

after.justification: V2 reports original model-specific task profiles, prompting ablations, jailbreak results, and transfer evaluations, including appendix results.

M1.justification: V2 adds post-generation dataset featurization: proposing features, clustering them, and selecting features using conditional perplexity to construct final task profiles (Section 2; Appendix H.8). V1 ends with generated questions and an updated model profile; its clustering experiment concerns seed retrieval. This substantially changes how the final outputs are constructed.

E1.justification: Both versions retain LegalBench/MAUD, forecasting consistency, TruthfulQA, HarmBench, cyberbullying, and cultural politeness. The four MAUD tasks, four politeness languages, 300 synthetic personas, and forecasting data sources remain the same. Expanded model comparisons and newly summarized failure patterns do not establish distinct dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 Figure 3 explicitly compares CoT, labels-only Graded, and Random conditions, whereas v1 Figure 3 displays adaptive versus randomized conditions with a static-accuracy reference. The direct static-versus-adaptive forecasting comparison in v1 Figure 6 is removed. PAIR and Report Cards remain evaluated comparators; newly discussed AutoBencher and Self-Challenge are related-work comparisons.

E3.justification: The context-size and evaluator-model sweeps are replaced by GPT-4o profiling five targets across three domains, and transfer model rosters change. V2 also reports a 50-prompt jailbreak comparison involving Sonnet 3.5 and Mixtral 8x7B. The earlier 30-question description remains in Appendix C.1, so its relationship to this comparison is unresolved; the PDFs do not establish matched reruns.

E4.justification: V2 substantially revises the CoT ablations and adds systematic model-specific failure analyses in Tables 4–9. It removes v1's generated-question validity study involving 20 human labelers and 20 TruthfulQA questions. Forecast extremization, forecasting optimization trajectories, and scaling to 160 politeness examples remain, largely relocated.

E5.justification: V2 removes the generated-question validation's agreement reporting, including majority agreement with the judge and average inter-annotator agreement. Both versions retain aggregation over five forecasts and the forecasting plots' variability bands. There is no newly documented increase in repeated runs or addition of confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: V2 adds task-by-model findings and replaces or expands ablation and transfer results. Its main jailbreak passage reports 32% versus 12% ASR under a 50-prompt setting, rather than v1's nearly 40% improvement claim; these are not established as comparable settings. Human-validity results disappear. V2 Figure 4's politeness panel reuses all 25 values from v1 Figure 7's forecasting panel after reordering and relabeling, leaving that result's attribution unclear.

T1.justification: The COND violation formula is algebraically unchanged: v2 abbreviates part of the denominator as D and moves the formula to Appendix A.2. Neither version presents theorems or proofs. The added featurization procedure is an algorithmic addition, without a new formal derivation or guarantee.

C1.justification: V2 centers the contribution on adaptive natural-language profiling and newly claims hundreds of task descriptions, an order of magnitude more than prior work. V1 emphasizes introducing Adaptive Evaluations, generating difficult questions, human validity, and transferability. Generalization and transfer claims remain, but the explicit human-validation claim is removed.

C2.justification: V2 interprets unelicited tasks as good model performance in Table 1, explains the choice of a different judge for Chinese politeness, and adds a dual-use risk-benefit argument. It removes v1's specific caveat about judge biases and limited human validation while retaining the limitations concerning small, noisy datasets and untested larger scales.

D1.justification: V2 adds implementation choices for featurization, including KMeans and Llama-3.1-8B perplexity scoring, and states that the persona dataset is released without providing an access link. It removes v1's judge-calibration description and filtering rates, and changes the token-cost example from 40 datapoints to approximately 50 successful questions. Most detailed prompts survive in Appendix H.

R1.justification: The positioning shifts from static benchmarking and adversarial evaluation toward combining dynamic benchmarks with qualitative profiling. V2 substantially discusses AutoBencher, Self-Challenge, VibeCheck, and other dynamic evaluation approaches, and introduces dataset featurization as a methodological foundation. Much of v1's redteaming and capability-elicitation discussion is retained in Appendix E.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method narrative, related work, and conclusion are substantially rewritten. The title changes from evaluating to profiling models, evaluator agents become profilers, and substantial methodological and related-work material moves into new appendices. The organization changes well beyond renumbering.

P2.justification: V2 changes the document from a single-column to a two-column layout, redraws the framework diagram, introduces task-by-model dot-matrix tables, and redesigns the ablation and transfer displays. The dataset summary loses model-role columns and moves to Appendix F. Several existing forecasting, scaling, and harassment figures are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: V2 clarifies task-profile construction and broadens the model analyses, but removes v1's human validation of generated questions. More seriously, its cultural-politeness transfer panel reproduces v1's forecasting values while changing the domain, axis roles, and DeepSeek-V3 label to Claude 3.5 Sonnet. These unresolved attribution problems weaken the expanded evidence. The gains in profiling and organization cannot be reliably weighed against the losses in validation and result traceability.
